correctness.rationale: At ≤4 original vertices all post-deletion graphs have ≤3 vertices, totally nested by edge inclusion up to relabeling, so one smallest residual graph is stochastically dominated at every p for all monotone component-size losses. For n=5 the exact distribution of the open cluster is sum over connected induced S with boundary closure (|S|/4)R(H[S],p)(1-p)^{b(S)}. The source verifier enumerates all 2^10 labeled graphs, 5! relabelings and 21 connected classes, compares all 105 delete-vertex objective polynomial pairs via two different expansions, and uses rational real-root isolation for inequalities on the whole interval. Both exceptional classes have exact mean/tail differences: A ΔM=p²(1-4p)/2, ΔT=p²(3-4p)/4; B ΔM=p²(p-1)(4p-1)/2, ΔT=p²(p-1)(4p-3)/4. Independent from-scratch enumeration reconstructed all 21 class representatives and those exact factorizations, and checked that only two classes disagree at p=1/2; full all-p claim rests on inspected exact source root-isolation certificates, not the finite check alone.

value.rationale: The distinction between expected total cases and probability of reaching a specified three-person harm threshold is a motivated risk-neutral versus risk-sensitive choice in stochastic network control. The complete first nontrivial graph-order boundary, two exact exception types and full disagreement interval are useful exact graph-reliability invariants not mechanically implied by the mean-only vaccination census.

final_claim: For one perfect vaccination, a uniform post-vaccination seed and independent homogeneous undirected bond percolation, the mean outbreak-size and ≥3-infection tail-risk objectives have a common optimal vaccinated vertex on every graph of order ≤4; among 21 connected five-vertex classes exactly two have disjoint optimizer sets, each precisely when 1/4<p<3/4.
limitations: Exact classification for connected five-vertex networks, any n≤4 including disconnected, p∈[0,1].
No claim for other risk thresholds, multiple vaccines, heterogeneous edges, or general Markovian SIR.
